name: Android NDK
description: Native development kit providing clang cross-compilers, sysroots and platform libraries for building C and C++ for Android ABIs.
limitations: Not available as a Termux package; Termux ships only ndk-sysroot
Full NDK is required to link real Android shared libraries

name: Android SDK Platform
description: Platform jar, aapt2, d8 and apksigner from the Android SDK build-tools. compileSdk and targetSdk values track the current platform release.
limitations: Full SDK is not packaged for Termux
License acceptance is interactive unless pre-seeded

name: Android SDK Build-Tools
description: aapt2, d8, zipalign and apksigner. These four tools are sufficient to assemble, align and sign an APK without Gradle.
requirements: Java runtime for d8 and apksigner
aapt2 binary for the host architecture
limitations: Termux packages are available but may lag the SDK release
apksigner requires a keystore for release builds

name: Android Gradle Plugin
description: Gradle plugin that drives Android builds. AGP 8.7 requires Gradle 8.9+ and JDK 17, and produces APK or AAB output with native library packaging.
limitations: Gradle is not installed in Termux by default
Daemon memory use is significant on low-RAM devices
Offline builds need a pre-populated dependency cache

name: Termux
description: Android terminal emulator and Linux environment without root. Provides bash, clang, rust, cmake, ninja, python and Java through its package manager, but not the full Android SDK/NDK.
requirements: Termux app from F-Droid or GitHub releases
limitations: No root, no systemd, no Docker
Android SELinux and W^X restrictions apply
Some packages are unavailable or outdated

license.name: GPL-3.0 for the app; packages vary

name: Termux ndk-sysroot
description: Termux package containing Android NDK sysroot headers and libraries for compiling C programs against bionic. It is not a full NDK and does not include the NDK build system or all platform libraries.
limitations: No standalone NDK toolchain files
Missing several platform libs and Vulkan validation layers
Not sufficient for a complete Gradle/NDK build

name: Java Native Interface (JNI)
description: Bridge between Java/Kotlin and native C/C++ code. The standard integration point for a Rust or C++ game core inside an Android app.
limitations: Every JNI call crosses a cost boundary; batch where possible
Global reference leaks crash the VM
Thread attachment is required for native-created threads

name: AAssetManager
description: Native API for reading assets packaged inside the APK. Required for streaming game data that is not unpacked to the filesystem.
requirements: AAssetManager_fromJava or the native asset manager from the app
limitations: Compressed assets need AAsset_openFileDescriptor or full reads
No random access to compressed entries
OBB files use a separate storage path

name: Opaque Binary Blob (OBB)
description: Expansion file format for game data larger than the APK limit. Files live under Android/obb/<package> and are read with a normal file path or the StorageManager.
requirements: Storage permission or app-specific OBB directory
limitations: Deprecated in favour of Play Asset Delivery
User must install both APK and OBB
Path layout differs across Android versions

name: Android Vulkan loader
description: System libvulkan.so loader that exposes the device Vulkan driver to applications. Linked with -lvulkan from the NDK.
limitations: Driver bugs are common on older devices
Validation layers are not present on production builds
Some devices report Vulkan but fail specific features

name: Scoped storage
description: Storage model restricting direct filesystem access. Apps use app-specific directories, MediaStore, or the Storage Access Framework.
requirements: App-specific external files dir for game data
READ_MEDIA_* permissions only for shared media
limitations: MANAGE_EXTERNAL_STORAGE is Play-restricted
Hard-coded /sdcard paths break
FileProvider is needed to share files
